title: Long vowels: ai ee ie oa oo
cando: read long vowel sounds written with two letters

about.text: In this lesson you learn the sounds ai, ee, ie, oa, oo. You hear each sound, you write its letters, and then you read words and a short text with them.
about.speech: In this lesson you learn five new sounds, and how to write them. You hear each sound, you write its letters, and then you read words and a short text with them.
goals: Say the sound for each new spelling
Read a word that has one in it
Write a word that has one in it
Know where in a word each one goes
Read the new words out loud

chapters.title: ai ee ie oa, and oo
chapters.text:
This is Lesson 9. The long vowels.
So far every vowel was short.
Cat. Pin. Dog. Bus. Short sounds.
Now the vowel says its own name.
Listen. Ai. That is the letter a, long.
Wait. w. ai. t. Three sounds.
Not four. The ai is one sound.
Rain. r. ai. n. Three sounds.
Next. Ee. That is e, long.
Feet. f. ee. t. Three sounds.
Listen to the pair. Fit. Feet.
Fit is short. Feet is long.
Next. Ie. That is i, long.
Pie. p. ie. Two sounds only.
Next. Oa. That is o, long.
Boat. b. oa. t. Three sounds.
Listen to the pair. Got. Goat.
Last. Oo. This one has two sounds.
Listen. Boot. Now listen. Foot.
Boot is long. Foot is short.
Same two letters. Two sounds.
You cannot tell by looking.
Try the long one first. Then the short one.
One of them will be a word you know.
Now three tricky words.
Who. Love. Have.
These do not follow the sounds.
Who is not w, h, o. It is hoo.
Love does not rhyme with the word rove.
Have does not rhyme with the word gave.
Learn those three by sight.
The vowel says its name.

sounds.about: Two letters, one sound: ai. It sits in the middle of a word.
Two letters, one sound: ee. It can sit in the middle or at the end.
Two letters, one sound: ie. It often comes at the end of a short word.
Two letters, one sound: oa. It sits in the middle of a word.
Two letters, one sound: oo. It has two sounds. Say the word and see.

reader.title: A Week of Rain
reader.text:
I had to wait a week.
Then I got on the boat.
It was wet. The rain did not stop.
I had wet feet in the boots.
A man on the boat had a pie.
He did not need it.
He said I can have it.
Who needs a wet pie? I do.

canDo: I can say the sounds ai, ee, ie, oa, oo.
I can read words like wait and feet.
I can write a word from its sounds.
I can read a short text out loud.
